standard_prerequisites.name: Sections over a quasi-compact object commute with filtered colimits with injective transition maps
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the commutation result to which both statements are reduced.

core_obligations: Recall that taking sections over W commutes with filtered colimits having injective transition maps, using the directed colimits lemma (proof lines 5351-5353).

Express a coproduct of sheaves of sets over an index set as the filtered colimit over the finite subsets of the finite coproducts, note that the transition maps are injective, and conclude statement (1) (proof lines 5354-5360).
Repeat the argument for a family of modules, using that a filtered colimit of abelian sheaves can be computed on sections, to obtain statement (2) up to line 5377 (proof lines 5362-5377).
proof_roadmap: Reduce coproducts to filtered colimits of finite coproducts.
Apply commutation of sections over a quasi-compact object with such colimits.
Repeat for modules using the description of filtered colimits of abelian sheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a quasi-compact object W of a site, the functor taking sections over W commutes with coproducts of sheaves of sets and with direct sums of modules. The proof rewrites a coproduct over an index set as the filtered colimit over the partially ordered set of finite subsets of the finite coproducts, whose transition maps are injective, and applies the known commutation of sections over a quasi-compact object with filtered colimits having injective transition maps (proof lines 5350-5377). The module case is handled the same way, using that a filtered colimit of abelian sheaves may be computed on sections. H2: the reduction of an arbitrary coproduct to a filtered colimit of finite ones, and the appeal to the directed-colimit lemma, are the substance.
